title: Infrastructure
description: Host CPU/memory/disk, containers, Postgres, uptime/TLS probes, nginx errors and the observability stack itself.

panels.title: CPU used
panels.description: Share of the VPS's total CPU in use (all cores). Amber above 70%, red above 90% — everything slows down.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Share of RAM in use (excluding reclaimable cache). Above 90% the kernel may kill containers (OOM).

panels.title: Lowest disk free
panels.description: Free space on the fullest real filesystem. Red below 10%: Postgres, Loki and Prometheus stop writing when the disk is full. Fix: docker system df, bun run docker:prune.

panels.title: Load (5m) per core
panels.description: Average number of processes waiting for CPU, divided by the number of cores. Below 1 = fine, above 1 = processes are queuing.

panels.title: CPU and memory
panels.description: Host CPU and memory used, in percent. Dashed lines at 70% and 90%.

panels.title: Disk free per mountpoint
panels.description: Free space on each real filesystem. Red below 10%, amber below 20%.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Processes waiting for CPU, averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, next to the number of cores. Load above the core count for long periods means the VPS is too small.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second in (received) and out (sent, shown below zero) on the host's network interfaces. A sudden huge spike in 'in' may be a bot flood.

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each compose service, as a share of one core (100% = one full core).

panels.title: Container memory
panels.description: Memory used by each compose service (working set — what counts towards OOM kills). A line that keeps growing until a restart means a leak.

panels.title: Postgres up
panels.description: Whether the Postgres exporter can connect to the database. DOWN = the API cannot work either.

panels.title: Connections used
panels.description: Open connections as a share of max_connections. Above 80% new connections may be refused.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size on disk of the application databases. Should grow slowly; a jump means a big import or bloat.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks in the selected range: two transactions blocked each other and Postgres killed one. Good: 0.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Open connections by state next to the max_connections limit.

panels.title: Rollbacks and deadlocks
panels.description: Transactions rolled back per second, and deadlocks. A few rollbacks are normal (failed validation); a sustained rise means queries keep failing — check the API error logs.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size on disk per database.

panels.title: Slow queries
panels.description: Statements slower than 500 ms logged by Postgres, per time bucket. Good: close to 0.

panels.title: Slow query log
panels.description: The slow statements themselves, with their duration. Use them to add indexes or fix N+1 queries.

panels.title: Probe status
panels.description: Whether each public URL answered successfully on the last probe (run from inside the VPS).

panels.title: Uptime (range)
panels.description: Share of successful probes per target in the selected range. Good: 100%.

panels.title: HTTP status
panels.description: HTTP status code returned to the last probe. Expect 200; 502/504 = nginx is up but the app behind it is not.

panels.title: TLS certificate expires in
panels.description: Days until the HTTPS certificate expires. Certificates renew automatically ~30 days before expiry; amber below 21 days, red below 7 days means renewal is broken.

panels.title: Probe latency
panels.description: How long the full probe took per target (DNS + connect + TLS + response). Good: under 500 ms; amber above 1 s.

panels.title: Probe success
panels.description: 1 = the probe succeeded, 0 = it failed. Gaps or drops to 0 are outages.

panels.title: nginx 5xx responses
panels.description: 5xx responses served by the web and english-quiz nginx containers. 502/504 here usually mean the API was down or restarting.

panels.title: nginx 5xx requests
panels.description: The failing requests: method, URI, status and time taken.

panels.title: Error lines by service
panels.description: Error/fatal log lines per service. The api, and any other service that logs JSON with a level field, is counted by its level label; the others (Postgres, nginx, Loki, Grafana…) by matching error words in the text.

panels.title: Error lines
panels.description: The error/fatal lines themselves, from every container, newest first.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Whether each metrics source (job) could be scraped on the last attempt. DOWN means that part of the dashboards will be empty — check the container of that name.

panels.title: Loki ingestion
panels.description: Log lines and bytes Loki receives per second. Dropping to 0 while containers run means Alloy stopped shipping logs.

panels.title: Prometheus storage
panels.description: Disk used by Prometheus' time-series database (blocks + write-ahead log). It is capped by the 30-day retention, so it should level off.
